sections.title: Basic maths (digits, primes, GCD, sieve)
sections.spot: Digit problems peel digits with `% 10` and `/ 10`; prime and divisor problems loop only up to sqrt(n); many queries call for a sieve.

sections.title: Recursion basics
sections.spot: Write each of these with recursion, not a loop: base case first, then trust the call on the smaller input.

sections.title: Sorting algorithms
sections.spot: Implement the named algorithm yourself; the answer is always the sorted array.

sections.title: Counting with merge sort
sections.spot: Count pairs (i < j) with some order condition: count them during the merge step of merge sort in O(n log n).

sections.title: Array basics (one pass)
sections.spot: One loop with a few variables (max, second max, count, previous value) is enough.

sections.title: Array tricks: voting, sum/XOR, cyclic sort
sections.spot: Values in a known range 0..n or 1..n, or "appears more than n/2 times": use sum/XOR maths, cyclic sort or Boyer-Moore voting instead of extra space.

sections.title: Matrix traversal
sections.spot: Work layer by layer or with boundary variables; do it in place when asked.

sections.title: Hashing and frequency counting
sections.spot: You need "how many times" or "have I seen this before": a HashMap or a count array.

sections.title: Two pointers
sections.spot: Sorted input, pairs or triplets, in-place compaction, or merging two sorted arrays: move two indices instead of nesting loops.

sections.title: Sliding window
sections.spot: Longest/shortest contiguous window with a condition, or "count subarrays with exactly K" (= atMost(K) - atMost(K-1)).

sections.title: Prefix sum + hashing
sections.spot: Subarray sum (or XOR) equal to K, with negatives allowed: store prefix values in a HashMap and look up prefix - K.

sections.title: Kadane's algorithm
sections.spot: Best contiguous subarray: keep the best answer ending at the current index.

sections.title: Binary search on a sorted array
sections.spot: Sorted (or rotated sorted) input and a target or boundary: halve the range each step.

sections.title: Binary search on the answer
sections.spot: "Minimum X such that it is possible" or "maximise the minimum": the yes/no check is monotonic, so binary search over the answer value.

sections.title: Binary search in 2D
sections.spot: Rows (and maybe columns) are sorted: binary search per row, start from a corner, or binary search on the value.

sections.title: Strings
sections.spot: Scan characters with indices, counters or a StringBuilder; parentheses problems keep a running depth.

sections.title: String matching (Rabin-Karp, KMP, Z)
sections.spot: Find a pattern inside a text in O(n + m), or questions about prefixes that are also suffixes (LPS / Z array).

sections.title: Bit manipulation
sections.spot: Single bits (`n >> i & 1`, `n & (n - 1)`), XOR cancelling pairs, or subsets as bitmasks.

sections.title: Subsets and subsequences (pick / not pick)
sections.spot: Every element is either taken or skipped: recursion with two branches per index.

sections.title: Backtracking
sections.spot: Build a candidate step by step, undo the step when you return (choose, explore, un-choose).

sections.title: Linked list basics (singly and doubly)
sections.spot: Pointer bookkeeping: handle the empty list, the head and the tail separately. Lists are shown as arrays in the examples.

sections.title: Linked list patterns (fast/slow, reverse, merge)
sections.spot: Middle or cycle: slow and fast pointers. Reorder: reverse part of the list. Combine sorted lists: merge.

sections.title: Stack and queue
sections.spot: Last-in-first-out matching (brackets, expressions, undo) or simulating one structure with another.

sections.title: Monotonic stack
sections.spot: "Next/previous greater or smaller element", or a sum over all subarrays of their min/max: keep a stack in sorted order.

sections.title: Monotonic deque
sections.spot: Max or min of every window of size k: a deque of indices, front = answer.

sections.title: Cache design (LRU / LFU)
sections.spot: O(1) get/put with eviction: HashMap + doubly linked list (LFU: one list per frequency).

sections.title: Greedy
sections.spot: A local best choice (largest ratio, earliest deadline, farthest reach) never hurts: sort, then take greedily.

sections.title: Intervals
sections.spot: Sort by start (merge, insert) or by end (pick the most non-overlapping); count overlaps with a sweep.

sections.title: Binary tree traversals and views
sections.spot: Visit nodes in a set order: DFS (pre/in/post) recursively or with a stack, BFS level by level with a queue, views by horizontal distance.

sections.title: Binary tree DFS: heights, paths, ancestors
sections.spot: Each node needs information from its subtrees (height, sum, found or not): return it from the recursion.

sections.title: Binary tree construction and conversion
sections.spot: Inorder splits left from right; preorder/postorder gives the root. Conversions re-wire pointers in a traversal.

sections.title: Binary search tree
sections.spot: Left < node < right: go one way per step (O(h)), and inorder gives sorted order.

sections.title: Heap implementation
sections.spot: An array where parent i has children 2i+1 and 2i+2; sift up after insert, sift down after removing the top.

sections.title: Top-K and K-way merge
sections.spot: "k largest / most frequent / closest" or "merge k sorted things": a heap of size k.

sections.title: Greedy with a heap or sorted map
sections.spot: A greedy rule ("always combine the two smallest", "always run the most frequent task", "always start from the smallest card") where a heap or TreeMap gives the next choice fast.

sections.title: Two heaps
sections.spot: Running median: a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half.

sections.title: Graph BFS / DFS and grids
sections.spot: Connected pieces, flood fill, "minimum steps" in an unweighted graph or grid: DFS for reachability, BFS for distance.

sections.title: Topological sort and directed cycles
sections.spot: Dependencies ("b before a"), ordering or a directed cycle: Kahn's BFS on indegrees or DFS with a path marker.

sections.title: Shortest paths
sections.spot: Weighted distances: BFS for unit weights, Dijkstra for non-negative weights, Bellman-Ford for negative edges, Floyd-Warshall for all pairs.

sections.title: Union-Find and minimum spanning tree
sections.spot: Groups that keep merging, or "connect everything at minimum cost": disjoint set union, Kruskal or Prim.

sections.title: Advanced graph algorithms
sections.spot: DFS discovery times and low-links (bridges, articulation points) or two DFS passes (strongly connected components).

sections.title: DP 1D
sections.spot: The answer at index i depends on a few earlier indices: dp[i] from dp[i-1], dp[i-2], ...

sections.title: DP on grids and 2D states
sections.spot: Moves through a grid or a day-by-choice table: dp[i][j] from its neighbours above/left (or the previous day).

sections.title: DP on subsets (knapsack family)
sections.spot: Choose items to reach a sum or capacity: dp[index][target]; unbounded versions may reuse an item.

sections.title: DP on strings
sections.spot: Two strings (or a string and its reverse): dp[i][j] over prefixes, compare the last characters.

sections.title: DP on stocks (state machine)
sections.spot: Buy/sell with rules: state = (day, holding or not, transactions left); I and II also have one-pass greedy answers.

sections.title: Longest increasing subsequence family
sections.spot: Pick a subsequence where each element "extends" the previous one: dp[i] = best chain ending at i (or patience sorting for length).

sections.title: Partition DP (matrix chain)
sections.spot: Try every split point k of a range i..j: dp[i][j] = best over k of dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + cost.

sections.title: Trie
sections.spot: Many prefix lookups, or maximum XOR (a trie over the bits).
